authorizes: nothing; this config has no runtime, no venue access, and no REAL_MONEY implication
descends_from: lane2_carry_hold_v1 (which stays registered and keeps scoring; v2 changes SIZING only)
claim: Same book as lane2_carry_hold_v1 (long top-100 Bybit names while their settled funding print is below -10 bp, hysteresis exit above -3 bp), but each held name's weight follows the premium actually being paid: w = 0.10 x clip(|trailing 24h settled funding| / 120 bp-per-day, 0.25, 1.0). Bet size proportional to edge. On corrected settlement-exact accounting over 2021-01..2026-07 this keeps v1's mean (17.0 vs 18.0 bp/day, paired daily differential -1.0 bp/day, t -0.4) while cutting max drawdown -60.0% -> -48.6%, raising Sharpe 1.02 -> 1.11, MAR 0.97 -> 1.25, and cutting turnover 27% (0.197 vs 0.271 one-way/day). This is a risk reallocation, not a mean claim.

universe.note: identical to v1; ranked within each decision bar, 168h price history required

state.signal: last settled funding rate at the decision bar (by_funding)
state.note: identical to v1. The per-PRINT entry is deliberately retained: the 2026-07-28 review's daily-rate entry variant (enter when trailing rate < -30 bp/day) collapsed to Sharpe 0.62 because distributed deep carry marks chronic decliners while a single deep print marks acute crowding; acuteness is load-bearing.

depth_scaling.note: w = cap x clip(|PIT trailing 24h settled funding| / ref, floor, 1.0). A name paying -120 bp/day or deeper holds full cap; carry decay shrinks the position smoothly instead of the v1 exit-or-full-size cliff; a missing trailing value sizes at the floor, never up. ref=120 is the middle of the flat region {100,120,160} (Sharpe 1.12/1.13/1.16), not the argmax; floor is flat across {0.15,0.25,0.35}.

sizing.gross_cap_note: unchanged from v1; the cap dilutes cascades instead of levering into them

risk.note: kept only for recipe comparability with v1. On corrected accounting the vol-target overlay HURTS both versions (v1 vt Sharpe 0.64 vs raw 1.02; v2 vt 0.52 vs raw 1.11; the backward-looking scale levers up after quiet stretches into crashes). RAW is the primary basis.

cost_model.charging: measured one-way turnover x fee per side, per day, identical to v1
cost_model.provenance: 7.78 bp/side measured 2026-07-25 from 85 forward demo fills (all taker)

scoring_recipe.metric: mean net bp per day and annualised Sharpe on the raw daily series (vol-targeted reported for recipe comparability, see risk.note)
secondary: paired daily differential net_bp(v2) - net_bp(v1) on shared days
scoring_recipe.comparator: lane2_carry_hold_v1's own forward rows on the same days (the paired differential isolates the sizing change), plus the deployed CONTINUOUS render and zero
scoring_recipe.cadence: one row per completed UTC day after the registration commit
scoring_recipe.eligibility: only days strictly after the registration commit date count as forward evidence

measured_at_registration.basis: CORRECTED settlement-exact scorer (2026-07-28), module path score_carry_hold; all numbers are seen-data Lane-1 selection, not evidence

robustness.basis_note: grid/robustness cells below were computed with the review scripts, whose trailing-rate windowing differs from the module on 50/1883 gap-adjacent days (module Sharpe 1.11 vs script 1.13 for this config); orderings are unaffected and the headline numbers above are module-path
robustness.declared_grid: ref {40,60,80} bp/day all improve v1 monotonically; POST-HOC extension {100,120,160} is flat (Sharpe 1.12/1.13/1.16) — no cliff
robustness.stale_entry_plus_1d: both books lose ~40% of mean (v1 18.0->10.4, v2 17.2->9.6 bp/day); v2 keeps its relative edge (Sharpe 0.82 vs 0.77). The first day after the signal carries the fat; +1h/+4h delays measured at v1 registration were free, +24h is not.
robustness.rejected_levers_same_review: trailing-rate EXIT tighten (flat), lagged-breadth gross tilt (hurts, DD window is itself high-breadth), daily-rate ENTRY (collapses, Sharpe 0.62), print-depth sizing (inferior to trail-depth: best cell Sharpe 1.02/MAR 1.16)

measured_at_registration.binance_replication: FAILS on the corrected scorer: same construction on Binance = +2.7 bp/day, t 0.4, Sharpe 0.18, MAR negative; depth sizing does not rescue it (0.16). v1's registered replication claim (Sharpe 1.38, effect ratio 0.50) was an artifact of the funding double-count. The mechanism is currently SINGLE-VENUE (Bybit) evidence.
measured_at_registration.multiple_testing: this review ran ~19 seen-data cells on top of the program's prior ~90 constructions; t 2.6 does NOT clear the program's historical Bonferroni-style bar (~3.4). v2 is a sizing refinement of an already-registered mechanism, not a new discovery; its evidence is the forward run and the paired differential vs v1.
measured_at_registration.provenance: Selected 2026-07-28 by the carry_hold quant review (docs/archive/2026-07-28-carry-hold-quant-review.md) on the corrected scorer over cross_venue_panel_v1 2021-01-01..2026-07-17 (seen data). Thesis tests T1-T6 preceded the grid; the grid was declared before any cell ran; the ref extension past 80 and the print-depth family are labelled post-hoc in the review.

known_weaknesses: inherits every v1 weakness: ~3.8 concentrated names when active, +0.75 correlation with financed_leaders, long-only market beta (contemporaneous BTC beta 0.44 on active days), capitulation entries can catch death spirals, capacity limited to the deep-negative-funding subset

REGIME BET vs v1: in shallow-carry grind years the smaller sizing gives up roughly half of v1's era mean (2023: 14.3 vs 26.0 bp/day) in exchange for the drawdown cut concentrated in deep-carry regimes (2025-26). If funding microstructure normalizes to 2023 shape, expect v2 to trail v1 while both stay positive
single-venue mechanism: the corrected Binance replication is ~zero; treat this as a Bybit-microstructure trade and re-examine if Bybit's funding interval mix or fee schedule changes
the vol-target overlay in the recipe is reported but harmful on corrected accounting (see risk.note); raw is primary
edge decays with signal staleness: +24h-stale entries lose ~40% of the mean; the daily decision cadence is the operating point, do not let scoring drift later
the -60% -> -44.6% drawdown cut is still a brutal drawdown for a raw book; nothing here makes the book deployable at full gross without separate owner-level sizing decisions
